subject: Clarify: model improvement opt-out, prompt/response custody & escrow flow
messages:
From: Sara Lawson <sara.lawson@elarahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elara Health Legal <legal@elarahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA questions: no-train commitment + custody for prompts/responses

Hi Rachel —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Before procurement moves forward we need clarity for our privacy team on a couple of items in the DPA and the security questionnaire: 

1) Model improvement / no-training: your DPA currently says Redwood will not use customer data to improve public model weights. Could you confirm how that applies to session-level telemetry and short-lived KV caches (are these entirely excluded from any training pipeline)? We need wording that covers both automated pipelines and any ad-hoc research uses.

2) Prompt/response custody: for certain regulated interactions we need an auditable custody path for prompts and generated responses (who has access, retention, and export paths). If Elara requests an escrow of interaction transcripts for audit, what mechanisms can Redwood support (SFTP export, secure onshore KMS storage, or DocuSign-style escrow)?

3) Subprocessors & cross-border transfer: if you rely on third-party inference runtimes or logging subsystems, what is the subprocessors list for the Dedicated tier and for Private (VPC) installs? Specifically: will any third party have persistent access to raw prompts?

I attached a marked-up DPA with our proposed language in the prompt/response custody section. We prefer a firm no-training commitment plus an operational export path if requested.

Appreciate any detail you can provide — our timeline is tight; procurement wants legal signoff this week.

Best,
Sara Lawson
Senior Privacy Counsel, Elara Health

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lawson <sara.lawson@elarahealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions: no-train commitment + custody for prompts/responses

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the clear summary and the redline. High-level answers below; I'll follow up with a short operations note and an export options matrix. We can iterate on exact contract language but want to be explicit before legal signs off.

1) No-training scope: Redwood will not use customer-provided prompts/responses to update public-facing model weights or to train new public models. This excludes (a) customer-requested opt-in programs and (b) aggregated telemetry used purely for performance/latency tuning (which is anonymized and cannot be traced back to customer interactions).

Operationally: session-level KV caches are transient (ephemeral by default) and are not routed to our model-training pipelines. Any permanent retention of prompts (for debugging or product features) is documented and requires an explicit customer opt-in. We can add a contract clause and an appendix that enumerates the operational guarantees (e.g., ephemeral TTLs, retention windows, audit logs) — Kimberly will draft.

2) Prompt/response custody & escrow: Redwood supports three export mechanisms:
  - Automated SFTP exports to a customer-controlled endpoint (encrypted in transit, sftp keys customer-managed)
  - Onshore KMS-backed object store snapshots (for Dedicated customers we can provision a residency-backed snapshot and provide read-only access keys)
  - Time-limited secure download via our Console with audit logging

For escrow: we can provide an encrypted archive staged to a Redwood escrow bucket that Elara may request be delivered to a named escrow recipient under a documented workflow (DocuSign workflow or direct transfer to escrow agent). We will provide chain-of-custody logs for any export/escrow operation.

3) Subprocessors: for Hosted/Standard we use a small set of cloud infra/logging providers — none have access to decrypted prompts unless required for incident response and only under strict access controls/auditing. For Dedicated we minimize subprocessors; for Private (VPC/on-prem) the control plane still lists a few subcontractors for telemetry ingestion but we can provide an on-prem distribution that eliminates remote access. Karthik, can ops produce the Dedicated vs Private subprocessors list and a short description of access controls?

Next steps: Kimberly will prepare suggested DPA language to close the loop on the no-train wording and an operational appendix. David will provide the subprocessor matrix. Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk legal through the export workflow?

Thanks,
Rachel
Director, Legal Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Sara Lawson <sara.lawson@elarahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elara Health Legal <legal@elarahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions: no-train commitment + custody for prompts/responses

Rachel —

Appreciate the quick answers. A couple clarifications from our side after internal review: 

• The procurement team needs the contract language to state explicitly that Redwood will not "use, access, or derivative-train" on Elara's prompts/responses for any model improvement without Elara's prior written consent. Wording like "will not use to improve or update models" is borderline; legal wants the slightly stronger phrasing above.

• On the export mechanics: for the escrow flow we require that any exported archive be encrypted with an Elara-managed key or delivered directly to an escrow agent's registered SFTP endpoint. We cannot accept a Redwood-managed decryptable copy sitting in a Redwood bucket without KMS separation.

I've attached inline comments to the redline; if Redwood can confirm the wording and the KMS/escrow behavior we can proceed to procurement approval. We can do a call tomorrow at 11am PT if that works.

Best,
Sara

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions: no-train commitment + custody for prompts/responses

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the precise language. Per Rachel's ask, I've drafted the contract-friendly clause and the operations appendix excerpts below (we'll push the full redline to the Doc):

Proposed DPA clause (suggested):
"Vendor shall not, and shall ensure its subprocessors do not, use, analyze, or otherwise process Customer Data to develop, improve, or update any machine learning or artificial intelligence models, weights, or training artifacts, except where Customer has provided prior written consent. Customer Data includes prompts, generated responses, session logs, and any derived metadata that can be associated with specific Customer accounts."

Operational appendix excerpt (key points):
- Ephemeral caches: KV caches are TTL-limited (default 30 minutes) and not persisted to training pipelines.
- Debug retention: Persistent retention for debugging requires explicit customer opt-in and is only stored in a customer-scoped, access-audited store.
- Export & escrow: Exports may be encrypted with a customer-provided public key; Redwood will deliver the encrypted archive to the customer-specified SFTP or escrow agent endpoint. Redwood will not retain a decryptable copy of escrowed archives beyond 7 days after delivery and will log the transfer event in the audit trail.
- Subprocessor access: The Dedicated offering: [list sanitized for thread] — no third party has direct persistent access to plaintext prompts. Private (VPC) deployments remove hosted telemetry routing; control-plane subprocessors are limited to SaaS billing/monitoring providers and operate on anonymized metrics where possible.

I'll attach a concise subprocessor inventory for Dedicated vs Hosted to the shared drive and the full clause redline in the Doc. Rachel — if you're happy with this language, I can push the redline to the Doc and join the 11am PT call tomorrow to walk through operations.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head, Privacy & Trust Operations — Redwood Inference
